AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO MENTAL HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the right to counsel for persons who receive services through the office of mental health or the office for people with developmental disabilities for certain investigations
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S7671

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the
right to counsel for persons who receive services through the office
of mental health or the office for people with developmental
disabilities for certain investigations

PURPOSE:

This bill amends paragraph (c) subdivision 25 of section 553 of the
executive law, providing a right to counsel, either through mental
hygiene legal service, or private financing, for individuals who are
recipients of OMH or OPWDD services, and are interviewed as part of a
Justice Center investigation.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill provides that individuals who are the recipients
of services through OMH or OPWDD licensed or operated services or
facilities, have a right to counsel when interviewed by, or on behalf
of, the justice center for the protection of people with special
needs.

Section 2 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

In pursuit of its mission, the Justice Center has been provided
substantial law enforcement and investigatory power. Recognizing that
numerous investigations involve people who we the recipients of
services, many of whom are vulnerable or underage and therefore may
the lack capacity to protect their own rights, it is imperative that
measures be taken to protect their legal rights in the investigation
process.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

An increase in costs for mental hygiene legal service can be
anticipated. In that the potential caseload cannot currently be
quantified, the exact amount cannot be calculated.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediately.

BILL NUMBER:S7671A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the
right to counsel for persons who receive services through the office
of mental health or the office for people with developmental
disabilities for certain investigations

PURPOSE:  This bill amends paragraph (c) and (d) of subdivision 25 of
section 553 of the executive law, providing a right to counsel, either
through mental hygiene legal service, or private financing, for
individuals who are recipients of OMH or OPWDD services, and are
interviewed as part of a Justice Center investigation. It also
requires notice to the parent, person in parental relation or legal
guardian, if any, of the person to be interviewed

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill provides that individuals who are the recipients
of services through OMH or OPWDD licensed or operated services or
facilities, have a right to counsel when interviewed by, or on behalf
of, the justice center for the protection of people with special
needs. It also provides for notice to the parent, person in parental
relation or legal guardian, if any of the person to be interviewed,
prior to the interview being conducted.

Section 2 is the effective date

JUSTIFICATION:  In pursuit of its mission, the Justice Center has been
provided substantial law enforcement and investigatory power.
Recognizing that numerous investigations involve people who are the
recipients of services, many of whom are vulnerable or underage and
therefore may the lack capacity to protect their own rights, it is
imperative that measures be taken to protect their legal rights in the
investigation process.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: 2014: New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  An increase in costs for mental hygiene legal
service can be anticipated. In that the potential caseload cannot
currently be quantified, the exact amount cannot be calculated.

EFFECTIVE DATE: Immediately.
